source.title: Ground-truth evaluation of sparse autoencoder features on spatial, single-cell and language-model embeddings
source.authors: Amirhossein Shahsavand; Shayan Forghani; Saba Akbarzadeh; Fatemeh Mahdavi Sabet

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether an SAE trained on a consensus-SAE residual recovers additional concepts. This is a different method from measuring whether SAE reconstruction error is linearly predictable or how its norms scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many results on feature reproducibility, concept coverage, and purity, but these do not measure SAE reconstruction error and are not rows for this claim. The rows below cover only the second-stage SAE experiments on residuals, which bear on V4's claim that further dictionary learning does not recover the residual's missed information.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It never measures SAE reconstruction error. Its 'residual' is the part of a biological or synthetic embedding left after a ridge fit on consensus-SAE codes, not a single SAE's error vector. It does not split that residual into linear and nonlinear parts, and it has no language-model residual-stage experiment. Its measures are reproducibility, concept coverage and purity, not error norms, loss or circuit faithfulness. The second-stage SAE result is a related construct (relearning what a seed consensus discards), so it goes under fits_no_version. The original dark-matter paper is not cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that what the consensus discards is mostly seed-specific detail rather than missed biology, since neither a compute-matched single fit nor a second-stage residual SAE recovered new concepts. They add that the consensus covers fewer lineages than single fits, and that all SAEs miss weak planted states that varimax recovers. They attribute that miss to the reconstruction objective weighting strong lineage variance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs, a five-fit consensus, and a second-stage SAE on a consensus residual. It does not measure linear predictability of SAE reconstruction error or per-token error scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Consensus reproducibility varied with dictionary size on Geneformer and with the amount of language-model data; these are not measurements of the claimed dark-matter properties.

fits_no_version.finding: Two settings were tested. On planted data (depth 500), a second SAE on the residual left by the consensus codes kept few reproducible features (0.17 ± 0.29) and raised weak-state recovery only from 0.17 to 0.28, within seed variation. On section B CellCharter (one seed), second-stage features reproduced at 0.29 and covered no lineage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information discarded by a multi-seed SAE consensus is mostly seed-specific detail that a second-stage SAE on the consensus residual cannot recover as new concepts.

record.problems: The residual-stage evidence is limited to the tested embeddings and concepts; the section B residual result uses one seed. The study does not measure the error properties in V1–V3 or V5–V6.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported reproducibility, feature-purity, rotation-baseline, or general coverage results directly measures SAE reconstruction error; see Results and Tables 1, S1, and S4–S5.

untested.parts: Whether SAE error is linearly predictable from the input; not measured.
Per-token error norms, their scaling across SAE sizes, and the overlap of failure contexts; not measured.
The effect of reconstruction on downstream loss compared with random errors; not measured.
The split of the error into linearly predictable and nonlinear parts, and whether either part resists further dictionary learning; not measured on SAE error.
Circuit or steering faithfulness with and without the error term; not measured.
Whether error shrinks with architecture or training choices. Matryoshka and BatchTopK are compared only on reproducibility and coverage.

record.verdict_notes: The study is about the reproducibility of SAE features on biological embeddings and Pythia-70m, compared against rotation baselines. The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed: no row measures SAE reconstruction error, and the residual-stage experiments are on non-language-model embeddings. The paper has no dark-matter framing.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE reconstruction error is a linear function of input activations.
Per-token error norms, their predictability across SAE sizes, overlap in contexts where differently sized SAEs fail, and whether error vanishes with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction replacements harm model loss more than equal-sized random errors.
The study tests recovery from a consensus-SAE residual, but does not separate linearly predictable from nonlinear error or establish that the residual is qualitatively different.
Whether SAE-based circuit or steering analyses lose model behaviour when the error term is omitted.
Whether dark matter is mainly an artifact of SAE training choices or shrinks with alternative architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: synthetic data, Expr50 embedding
rows.operation_detail: Trained a second-stage consensus SAE on the residual of the anchored consensus SAE.
rows.measure: Share of weak planted states recovered
rows.note: The authors say the increase was within seed variation, and conclude the second-stage model did no better.
rows.check: The residual is of a linear fit on consensus codes over a synthetic Expr50 embedding, not SAE reconstruction error, and there is no linear/nonlinear split, so the row does not measure V4. On its own measure, weak-state recovery rose from 0.17 to 0.28, which the authors call within seed variation, so 'absent' rather than 'observed'.

rows.subject: synthetic data, Expr50 embedding
rows.operation_detail: Trained a second-stage consensus SAE on the residual of the anchored consensus SAE.
rows.measure: Share of weak planted states recovered
rows.note: The authors say the increase was within seed variation, and conclude the second-stage model did no better.
rows.check: Same as R1 (25% second-stage consensus: 0.17 to 0.28, within seed variation). Second-stage features reproduced at 0.17 ± 0.29 and only 3.7 of 50 were kept; combined R1 was 0.85.

rows.subject: CellCharter embedding of section B
rows.operation_detail: Trained a second-stage SAE on the residual of the consensus SAE.
rows.note: The residual SAE did not recover a lineage in this setting.
rows.check: Not SAE reconstruction error, and the subject is a CellCharter embedding rather than a language model. The baseline should be stage-1 coverage: 4.3 lineages (anchored) per Table S5. Second-stage features reproduced at 0.29 and covered no lineage (one seed).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Planted data at depth 500 and section B CellCharter residual
reader_labels.reason: Second-stage SAEs recovered no additional lineage in section B, and the weak-state recovery increase on planted data was described as within seed variation; see R1–R3. This supports resistance to further dictionary learning in these tested settings, but not the claimed distinction between linear and nonlinear error.
